AIcoach UX exploration

AIcoach Round 3

Ten variations inside the direction Chris chose: concept 06 "The Coach Talks" as the base (colours, wordmark, type), the calm and low text density of concept 09, and the skeleton golfer with keypoints from concept 02. The ten share one identity and differ in layout, hierarchy and interaction pattern.

Use By page to compare all ten on the same screen, for example the result page.

01Faithful Merge02Verdict First03One Thing Per Screen04Skeleton Hero05Frame + Conversation06Quiet Paper07Stage Bands08Tray and Sheets09Timeline Spine10Coach Card Stack
01

Faithful Merge

06's conversation at 09's pace: same thread, Evidence panel and cards, each holding less. The panel shows 2 key frames and the one measurement.

Concept notes

Idea: 06's conversation, told at 09's pace. The thread, the Evidence panel and the cards stay where they were in 06. Each one now holds less.

What came from where

  • 06, The Coach Talks (structure and identity): the palette, the wordmark and coach mark, Newsreader, Figtree and IBM Plex Mono, and the text sizes. The layout keeps 06's three parts: a left rail, the thread and the sticky Evidence panel. The coach speaks in serif. Measured numbers are mono teal with [n] pins. Dashed outlines mean inferred. The verdict, fault chain, practice and "Also checked" arrive as structured cards inside the thread, and a "Jump to" chip bar indexes them. Upload is a message, the composer is the drop zone, and the analysis appears as a step log in the thread. The grounding note sits under every composer.
  • 09, Cairn (calm): each card does one job. Coach messages are one or two sentences. The full explanation is hidden behind "Read my full explanation · 118 words". On the phone, the result shows the verdict, the 7%, the two frames and the feel cue. Practice is one tap away ("Next: what to practise"). The secondary pages follow 09's contact sheet: one idea per phone, with actions in the thumb zone.
  • 02, Lab Instrument (figure only): the key frames reuse 02's pose geometry: ghost body capsules, keypoint dots and connecting lines. Body lines are #8ED3E6 on the #36312B ground. The hip keypoint is ringed. The impact frame overlays the dashed address pose and a "+7%" dimension arrow from the address hip line. There is no graph paper and there are no axes.

Removed to stay simple

  • Evidence panel: 06 had 6 pins and a clip timeline. Here it has 2 key frames and 1 measurement (7%). Pins 4–6 are folded into "3 more measurements", and the clip checks are folded into one "passed 3 of 3" row.
  • The verdict card no longer repeats the key frames, since they are already in the panel. Its threshold ruler moved to the panel.
  • The explanation paragraph is collapsed by default. The upload exchange collapses to one "Clip received" line.
  • "Also checked" drops 06's posture ruler. Each fault gets two lines, and the possible fault stays visible.
  • The checklist items lost their sub-descriptions on the phone. The landing page has six sections, each with one claim.

Risks

  • Folding the explanation and pins 4–6 behind disclosures saves space, but the "why" now depends on one tap. Players who skim may never open the 118-word explanation.
  • Keeping 06's three columns still gives a busy frame at 1280 px, even with less inside. The Evidence panel probably needs to collapse into a drawer on narrow laptops, as 06 also noted.
02

Verdict First

One calm verdict screen with a large impact key frame. "See why" and "What to practise" open the coach beside it only when asked.

Concept notes

Idea: The result opens on one calm verdict screen: fault name, a one-line feel cue, confidence and the impact key frame drawn large. There are exactly two ways on, "See why" and "What to practise". The coach conversation is a second layer that opens beside the verdict (desktop) or as a sheet under it (phone), only when asked.

This answers the risk in 06 that chat-as-frame is slow. Rory gets the answer in one glance, and the conversation is still one tap away.

Taken from 06 / 09 / 02

  • 06: the whole visual language (palette, coach mark and AIcoach wordmark, Newsreader / Figtree / IBM Plex Mono, text sizes). The coach speaks in serif with its mark. Measured values are mono teal, with pin [1] linking the "+7%" on the frame to its caption and the "Based on" footnote. Dashed means inferred: the likely-cause node, the unverified observation and the verdict slot that is still waiting. The grounded-chat lock note is kept. Upload stays a coach message: the checklist is its message and the composer is the drop zone. The analysing state streams in as a step log.
  • 09: one idea per screen, actions in the thumb zone on the phone, short copy, and progressive disclosure (verdict → why → practise → ask). The secondary pages are single-purpose phone frames. Every outcome uses the same verdict shape: label, one name, one line, at most two actions. That includes Cannot analyse and No verified fault found.
  • 02: the pose skeleton (keypoint dots and connecting lines, built from 02's coordinates), restyled as 06 body lines #8ED3E6 on key-frame ground #36312B. Faint body capsules stay behind it. The impact frame overlays the dashed address pose and a "+7%" dimension from the address backside line.

Removed to stay simple

  • 06's left conversation rail, its sticky Evidence panel, its "Jump to" chip bar, and the long thread of structured cards on the result page.
  • The fault chain, the possible fault and the clip checks are not on the first screen. They live under "See why" (the verdict carries only a one-line "Also checked").
  • The landing page has no fault table. Three small cards replace it.

Risks

  • With two buttons and the chat hidden, some players may never open "See why" and so miss the likely cause and "Loss of posture: possible". The one-line "Also checked" has to stay on the verdict.
  • The chat is now secondary, so the grounded coach may feel less like the product. It is reached only through the two layers, and on the phone only from the sheet.
03

One Thing Per Screen

Four calm steps (Fault, Why, Practise, Ask the coach), each opened by the coach's sentence, with the chat one tap away from every step.

Concept notes

Idea: The result is four calm steps (Fault, Why, Practise, Ask the coach). Each step is its own screen, the coach's sentence opens it, and the chat is one tap away from every step.

What came from where

  • 06 (skin): the full palette, Newsreader / Figtree / IBM Plex Mono at 06's sizes, the flag-mark and AIcoach wordmark, the clay coach label, mono-teal measured values with numbered evidence pins ([2] impact frame, [3] hip movement), dashed outline only for the inferred likely cause and the unverified observation, and the grounded-chat note under the composer. The landing keeps 06's hero line and its honesty section.
  • 09 (structure): the most 09-like part of round 3. Phone first, one main thing per screen, a step bar at the top, the primary action in the thumb zone, and "Also checked" moved into a sheet instead of shown up front. Upload is four phones: film, ready, analysing, then "your answer is ready" as a short contents page of the four steps.
  • 02 (figure): the key frames use 02's skeleton construction (keypoint dots joined by lines, faint body capsules behind), recoloured to #8ED3E6 on #36312B. The hip keypoint is ringed because it is the measured point. The drill illustration uses the same skeleton in ink on paper.

Step rules

  • Every step opens with Coach plus one serif sentence. On Why, the feel cue is that sentence.
  • "Ask the coach about this" sits under every step. It opens step 4 with that step as context. The thread itself only lives in step 4.
  • The step bar adapts to the result: Nelly's no-fault result has only Result · Ask, and a rejection has no step bar.
  • On desktop, the steps form one vertical stepper. One step is open, and the others fold to their coach sentence. Once a step is done, it folds to a one-line summary of facts.

Removed to stay simple

06's left conversation rail, the persistent Evidence panel, the "Jump to" chip bar, the swing-event timeline and the clip checks. The full explanation sits behind "Read my full explanation". The possible fault, the fault not found and the save toggle are in the "Also checked" sheet. The upload drop zone has a solid outline so that dashed lines keep meaning only "inferred".

Risks

  • Four taps to reach the chat can feel slow for returning players who only want the verdict. The contents page and "ask straight away" link help, but a compact summary view may be needed.
  • With the Evidence panel gone, the pins on later steps point back to step 1 instead of staying visible. That keeps the screens calm but asks the player to remember or go back.
04

Skeleton Hero

The pose figure carries the page: your own skeleton is the result, and every measurement is pinned to the keypoint it came from.

Concept notes

Idea: The pose figure carries the page. Your own skeleton is the result, and every measurement sits on the keypoint it was measured from.

What I took, and how

  • From 06 (main language): all of the palette, the mark and wordmark, Newsreader for the coach's voice, Figtree for the UI, and IBM Plex Mono only for measured values. Teal numbered pins, dashed outlines for inferred items, the coach tag, the clay CTA and the grounded-chat lock note all come from 06 too. The landing headline is the 06 headline, and the upload page keeps 06's "coach asks for one clip" wording and its step log.
  • From 09: one idea per section and per phone screen, short copy, and progressive disclosure ("Read the full explanation", "Also checked" folded into two quiet rows). Actions sit low on the phone in thumb reach. The result runs Fault, Why, Practise, Ask, the same order as 09's stepper.
  • From 02: the figure construction, rebuilt from 02's key-frame keypoint coordinates (head, neck, shoulder, elbow, hands, hip, knee, ankle, toe, heel, club, ball, in body-height units). It is restyled for 06: key-frame ground #36312B, body lines #8ED3E6, a faint body mass in #4A433A, the address pose as a dashed ghost, and a clean dimension line for the 7% hip shift.

Signature moves

  • Landing hero = a film strip. Three frames (address, top, impact) share one dashed address-hip line, so you can see the hip leave the line at impact (7% [3]).
  • Result hero = one big figure. The impact skeleton sits over the faint address skeleton with the hip shift as a dimension line. Evidence pins are small cards attached to keypoints: [3] hips toward the ball, [4] lead hip turn, [5] posture angle. Pins [1] and [2] are the two frames. A timeline scrubber (address, top, impact) runs along the floor of the frame. The coach's words sit beside the figure.
  • Analysing = the figure draws itself. Keypoints appear, bones join, and the dimension line shows as "measuring…" until its pin lands.
  • The chat points back at the figure. A small copy of the figure sits beside the conversation. The pins the answer cites are lit, and the rest are outlined.
  • The same figure tells the honest outcomes. Cannot analyse shows feet cut off by the frame edge. No verified fault shows Nelly's hips staying on the line with no pins.

Removed to stay simple

06's left conversation rail and its sticky Evidence panel (the pins now live on the figure). The "Jump to" chip bar became four quiet tabs. The fault chain lost its prose, and the explanation sits behind a disclosure link. Posture and Over the top are one line each. 02's graph paper, axis ticks, IDs and error bars are gone, and so are 09's cairn stones.

Risks

  • Pin cards on the figure can cover joints on narrow screens. The phone uses bare numbered pins (tap to open), so that interaction has to be built and tested.
  • A large, exact-looking skeleton can suggest more precision than 2D pose delivers. The confidence words and the dashed "inferred" convention have to stay visible next to every pin.
05

Frame + Conversation

Two calm columns: a sticky dark stage shows the swing, the coach talks beside it, and every pin the coach cites makes the stage jump to that frame.

Concept notes

Idea: Two calm columns. A sticky dark stage on the left shows the swing, and the coach talks on the right. When the coach cites a pin, the stage jumps to that frame and lights the keypoint.

What I took

  • From 06 (main design): all of it. Palette, the mark and wordmark, Newsreader for the coach / Figtree for the UI / Plex Mono for measured values only, numbered teal pins, "dashed = inferred", the grounded composer note, and the upload as a coach message with a dashed drop zone. 06's key-frame ground #36312B becomes the whole stage column, not a thumbnail.
  • From 09: one main thing per section, short copy, progressive disclosure (the full explanation folds away, "Also checked" is one quiet card), and big thumb-zone buttons on the phone. The secondary pages use one idea per frame.
  • From 02: the figure construction. Ghost body capsules, bone lines and ringed keypoints, using 02's body-height coordinates (hip −0.04 → +0.03 BH = 7%). It is redrawn in #8ED3E6 on the dark stage. A cited keypoint gets a ring and a halo.

Signature

  • The stage follows the talk. Inline evidence chips (7% of body height [3], impact frame [2]) are tinted #E2ECEC. When the coach's answer cites one, the stage jumps to that frame and lights the hip, and a matching tinted chip on the stage reads "Cited in the latest answer".
  • Address · Top · Impact scrubber under the frame, with the clip's timeline above it.
  • The stage has one job on every page. It shows the frame the coach needs (upload), then your clip, then the frame being measured (analysing), and later the bad clip (rejection), Nelly's top frame (no fault) and the selected swing (library).
  • Phone: the stage shrinks to a 196 px slim frame pinned under the header. Tapping it opens the stage full screen.

Removed to stay calm

06's left rail of conversations (now just top-bar links), the third evidence column, the "Jump to" chip bar, the fault-chain card grid (now a three-line vertical chain), clip checks on the result, and the inline full explanation (folded away).

Risks

  • Hiding evidence in the stage means only one frame shows at a time. Comparing address and impact side by side relies on the dashed address line and the scrubber.
  • On 1280 px laptops the 620 px stage squeezes the conversation column. The stage may need to shrink to about 480 px, or collapse into the slim frame, below about 1200 px.
06

Quiet Paper

One centred column of paper, about 40 words per section; evidence stays hidden until you tap a pin, then opens in place.

Concept notes

Idea: The most minimal version of the family. One centred column of paper, with type and whitespace doing the work. The evidence stays hidden until Rory taps a pin, and then it opens in place.

Text budget

The hard limit is about 40 visible words per screen section: a heading, at most two short sentences, and the confidence word. Three things fall outside the limit, and each is noted where it appears:

  • copy that must be there (the mobility safety note and the swing-library consent line);
  • an evidence panel after the player opens it;
  • one coach chat answer, which gets its own budget of about 40 words.

Layout rules

  • Desktop uses one reading column, 640 px wide and centred. There are no side panels, chip bars, cards or rails.
  • A section is separated from the next by whitespace (150–230 px) and a small uppercase label. Rules and outlines are not used for this.
  • Only three kinds of border remain:
  • the dashed outline, which means inferred or unverified;
  • the phone bezel;
  • outline buttons.
  • The landing page has 4 sections: thesis, one example result, "When it can't tell, it says so", and "Film. Send. Read." with the CTA.

Taken from the sources

  • 06: the full palette, the wordmark geometry and the type roles. Newsreader is the coach (headlines, coach lines, the clay feel cue), Figtree is the UI, and IBM Plex Mono in teal is used only for measured values, each with a [n] pin. Also kept: dashed = inferred, the grounded chat note ("Answers are based only on this analysis") and the "Based on:" footnote.
  • 09: one idea per section, short copy, actions in thumb reach on the phone, and phone screens with one main thing each. "Also checked" is shown in full on the result page, so nothing is hidden behind a step.
  • 02: the pose model. The keypoint coordinates come from 02's address and impact plots. Here the figure is drawn in ink on paper, with soft paper-2 body capsules, a teal hip keypoint, a dashed address-hip line and a dashed address ghost pose. The impact frame shows the 7 % gap as a teal arrow. During analysis the same skeleton draws itself as each step finishes.

Removed to stay simple

  • 06's Evidence panel, left rail, "Jump to" chips, card frames, message bubbles for the coach and the step log detail.
  • The chain cards became a three-node vertical line: a dashed node for the likely cause, a solid node for the measurement and a filled node for the verified fault.
  • The suggested prompts became two plain text links.
  • The key frames sit on paper and do not use the dark key-frame ground.

Honesty kept

Every confidence band shows its word and its 3 bars. Every measured number is mono teal with a pin. Pins open the key frames, the value, the threshold and the band inline. The "possible" and "not found" checks stay visible. Nelly's unverified observation is the only dashed box on her page.

Risks

  • The page gets long. With this much whitespace, the result page runs to about 3,800 px, and a player who stops scrolling may never reach "Also checked" or the chat. A sticky "Ask the coach" link may be needed.
  • Hidden evidence relies on people noticing the small [1] pins. If they never tap one, they see the verdict without the proof. The first pin may need to open by default on the first visit, as drawn here.
07

Stage Bands

Dark bands whenever the page shows your swing, light paper whenever the coach talks or you act: one idea per band.

Concept notes

Idea: The page has two kinds of full-width band. When it shows the swing, the band is dark (06's key-frame ground #36312B with #8ED3E6 skeleton lines). When the coach talks or you act, the band is light paper. Each band holds one idea.

How the rhythm works

  • Landing: the bands tell the story. Paper hero, then a dark band (1 · Film: phone on a stand, golfer at address), paper (2 · Upload: one card, one button), dark (3 · Answer: what it measured, with the address and impact key frames and 7%), paper (3 · Answer: what the coach says, with the feel cue and a short "ask why" exchange), dark (the three faults, one figure each), paper (honest answers and the grounded-chat refusal), and a quiet paper-2 call to action at the end.
  • Upload: the coach's request sits on paper. A dark band follows with the six filming essentials drawn onto the set-up (hand height line, 2.4–3.7 m, frame brackets, and pills for 120 fps and one swing). The drop zone is on paper. While it analyses, the dark band shows address, top and impact frames as their body lines are drawn, on a timeline. The five steps tick off on paper.
  • Result: the verdict is on paper. Then one dark band holds the key frames and the single measurement that matters (7% against the 4% rule, confidence high). After that everything is paper: why it happens (feel cue, explanation, vertical fault chain), what to practise, a collapsed "Also checked" section, and the chat. The chat shows the cited impact frame as a small dark tile.
  • Phone: each screen opens on a dark swing band and ends on paper, with one action in thumb reach.

Taken from

  • 06: palette, Newsreader/Figtree/IBM Plex Mono and their sizes, the mark and wordmark, coach label, measured values in mono teal with [n] pins, dashed = inferred, the grounded-chat note and "Based on" footnote, and the clean drop-zone layout from 02-upload.
  • 09: one idea per band or screen, short copy, big thumb-zone buttons, progressive disclosure (only the 7% is on the result's stage band, and "Also checked" is collapsed to one line per fault).
  • 02: the pose model. Keypoint dots and connecting lines use 02's exact address and impact coordinates, with faint body capsules (line colour at 11%). On impact, the dashed address ghost and the hip-gap arrow are kept. They are restyled as #8ED3E6 on #36312B, with no graph paper.

Removed to stay simple

06's three-column shell (rail, thread, sticky evidence panel). The 31°, 6° and hand-path measurements are no longer on the result's stage; they live in the chain and in "Also checked". The "Jump to" chips, the clip-check list on the result, the separate swing-events log and the drill pictograms are gone. Only body movement is drawn, and always on dark.

Risks

  • A long run of full-width dark bands can feel heavy or cinematic on a phone in sunlight at the range. The bands must stay short, and paper must always carry the action.
  • The rule "dark = swing" only works if it is strict. One dark band used for decoration (for example, a dark call to action) would break the meaning, and the swing-library thumbnails stretch it a little.
08

Tray and Sheets

The coach thread is the base layer; evidence, practice and the chat slide up as bottom sheets at peek, half and full, and become one right-side drawer on desktop.

Concept notes

Idea: The coach thread is the base layer. Everything else (evidence, practice, the chat) slides up over it as a bottom sheet with fixed heights, so one thing is in front at a time and Rory always gets back the same way: drag down.

Sheet states (phone, 390 × 844)

HeightpxUsed by
Peek132One dock: the Evidence tray row (pin count and thumbnails) above the composer field. Always present on a result.
Half460Clip sheet (upload), Evidence tray after a pin tap (key frames and that one value), Practice sheet (Wall drill), filming-guide step, every confirmation.
Full780Evidence tray with all six pins, Practice sheet on the Mobility tab, Ask sheet (grounded chat).

The Practice sheet has no peek: you open it, you don't browse it. The Ask sheet skips half because a conversation needs the room. On desktop the tray and the practice sheet become one right-side drawer (tabs Evidence · Practise) that is closed by default and pushes the thread left without covering it. The composer stays docked in the thread there.

What I took

  • From 06: the full palette, Newsreader/Figtree/IBM Plex Mono and their text sizes, the wordmark and flag mark, the serif coach voice, mono teal values with numbered pins, dashed outlines for inferred links, the grounded-chat lock note, the "upload is a message" idea (the composer becomes the clip chooser or drop zone), and the evidence tray from 06's phone version, promoted here to the main interaction.
  • From 09: the calm upload flow (film one swing → ready when you are → analysing → answer ready), one idea per screen, actions in the bottom third, short copy, and confirmations as sheets.
  • From 02: the pose model. Address and impact are skeletons with keypoint dots and connecting lines (02's geometry, re-projected), drawn as #8ED3E6 lines on the #36312B key-frame ground. The hip keypoint is ringed, the address hip is a dashed line, and the impact frame carries a dashed address ghost and a +7% arrow. The Wall drill reuses the same skeleton in ink on paper, with the hip in clay against the wall.

What I removed to stay simple

  • The left conversation rail, the "Jump to" chip bar and the always-open Evidence column from 06's result page.
  • The full explanation (only two sentences show; the rest is behind "Read the full explanation"), the possible fault and the not-found fault (collapsed into one "Also checked" row), and the clip checks (one line inside the tray).
  • Repeated numbers. 7% appears once in the thread and once in the tray, not on every card.

Risks

  • Sheets hide things. A player who never drags the tray up never sees the key frames, so the peek row has to keep showing the thumbnails and the pin count.
  • Two layers at peek (tray row above the composer) is a dense 132 px. It needs real-device testing for mis-taps, and the gesture rules (drag versus tap) must stay identical on every sheet.
09

Timeline Spine

The swing's own timeline (address, top, impact) is the spine of the result, and every finding hangs on the moment it comes from.

Concept notes

Idea: The swing's own timeline is how you move through the result. A slim track holds three skeleton thumbnails (address 0.86 s, top 1.80 s, impact 2.07 s), and every finding hangs on the moment it comes from.

How it works

  • Result: On desktop the track runs horizontally. Impact carries the measured value (7% of body height [3], rule 4%, confidence: high) beside its frame, with the dashed "likely cause" note below it. Address carries the hip line reference, and top carries "Over the top: not found". The explanation, the drill and the mobility exercise come below. "Also checked" is one quiet line.
  • Chat: Answers link to a moment with a chip ("Impact · 2.07 s"), and the timeline highlights that moment in evidence tint. The drill card links to a moment in the same way ("Feel it at impact").
  • Analysing: The same track fills in as the steps finish. Pose draws the bodies, swing events pin the times, measurements attach to their moments, then the rule table and explanation follow. Before upload the spine is three dashed placeholders.
  • Phone: The spine turns vertical down the left edge, with notes to the right. The chat sheet keeps a mini horizontal timeline above it.
  • Honest states: For "Cannot analyse", the spine is dashed and empty, and each reason hangs where the clip broke (whole clip, address, impact) with a link to the filming guide step. For Nelly's swing, the spine is calm and the only note is a dashed, low-confidence unverified observation at the top. In the swing library, every row is a tiny three-dot spine with the finding moment in teal.

Taken from

  • 06: The full palette, Newsreader/Figtree/Plex Mono and their roles, the mark and wordmark, mono teal values with [n] pins, dashed outlines for inferred findings, the grounded-chat lock note, card style and the composer.
  • 09: One idea per section or screen, short copy, progressive disclosure ("Read the full explanation", "Also checked"), full-width thumb-zone actions and the phone contact sheet.
  • 02: The skeleton construction (keypoint dots, bone lines, quiet body capsules, the club line and a dashed address hip line on impact), using 02's body-height coordinates and redrawn as #8ED3E6 on #36312B.

Removed to stay simple

06's evidence panel, the left conversation rail, the jump-to chips, the full fault-chain card, the threshold ruler, the clip-checks list and the four-pin evidence list. On the result page, the measured value sits at its moment instead.

Risks

  • Top and impact are only 0.27 s apart, so the track is spaced evenly rather than to scale. The times are shown in mono, but the spacing is not proportional.
  • Findings that span moments (loss of posture compares downswing with address) do not fit one node cleanly. They fall back to the "Also checked" line.
10

Coach Card Stack

The answer arrives as four calm cards in one column (What I saw, Why it happens, This week's practice, Ask me), each opened by the coach in serif and folded to one line when done.

Concept notes

Idea: The coach answers in a short stack of large, calm cards in one column. Each card holds one idea (What I saw, Why it happens, This week's practice, Ask me), opens with the coach's voice in Newsreader, and folds to a single line when you are done with it.

It sits between 06's thread and 09's one-screen-per-step. It has the order and the voice of a conversation, but each part of the answer stays in a fixed place.

What I took, and how

  • From 06 (main design): the palette, wordmark and coach mark, the Newsreader, Figtree and IBM Plex Mono roles, and 06's text sizes. The card surface is 06's: the card colour, a hairline, and a faint offset shadow. Measured values are mono teal with numbered pins (1–2 key frames, 3–4 measurements). Dashed means inferred and solid means measured. The landing keeps 06's hero, its "rules" band, the fault table, the "says no" trio and the dark call-to-action band. The grounded chat keeps its lock note and "Based on" line.
  • From 09: one idea per card, progressive disclosure, short copy, and every phone action in the bottom third. The other-pages sheet is a set of one-idea phone frames. Confirmations open inside the card, never in a pop-up.
  • From 02: only the figure. It is the pose skeleton with keypoint dots and lines, using 02's address and impact coordinates. Body lines are #8ED3E6 on the #36312B key-frame ground, with the body mass toned into the ground. The hip keypoint is emphasised, and a dashed line marks where the hips were at address. On the impact frame, a +7% arrow shows how far they moved.

The card grammar (used on every page)

  • Collapsed: mark, card title (Figtree), a one-line summary in Newsreader, and a chevron.
  • Expanded: the same header, then a Newsreader opener, then the content.
  • Ghost (dashed): a card the coach has not earned yet. While the clip is analysed, Why, Practice and Ask wait as dashed outlines and fill in as the steps finish.
  • The filming guide, library, rejection, no-fault and account pages are the same stack. The filming steps, the saved swings and the account sections are all folded cards that open in place.

What I removed to stay simple

06's left conversation rail, the sticky Evidence panel, the "Jump to" chips, the clip-checks list and the fault-chain boxes (now a vertical node chain with no nested boxes). The possible fault and over the top are two quiet lines under "Also checked", and the second figure overlay is gone (only the hip line remains). The desktop result is one 760 px column with empty margins.

Risks

  • Folded cards hide content. A player who never opens "Why it happens" misses the cause. The one-line summaries have to carry the gist, and the first card always arrives open.
  • Four similar cards can feel like a form. The serif opener in each card and the strict one-idea rule are what keep the stack conversational. If either slips, it turns into a settings page.
